review_notes: I read the whole file and compared it with Mathlib's Kronecker material. That covered `Matrix/Kronecker.lean` and `Matrix/GeneralLinearGroup/Defs.lean` (`Matrix.IsUnit.kronecker`, `GeneralLinearGroup.kronecker`), plus the `mul_kronecker_mul` and `kronecker_one` lemmas. The file adds no new definitions, structures or classes. It has only theorems and one private helper lemma. `Matrix.IsUnit.kronecker` needs a `CommSemiring`, and `mul_kronecker_mul` also needs commutativity. Mathlib has no noncommutative or rectangular `NonAssocSemiring` version of the factorization `(A ⊗ₖ 1) * (1 ⊗ₖ B) = A ⊗ₖ B`. So `kronecker_one_mul_one_kronecker` and `isUnit_kronecker` are strict generalizations, not competing versions of an existing concept. The file also ties itself to Mathlib: `GeneralLinearGroup.isUnit_kronecker_unit` shows the extracted unit equals `GeneralLinearGroup.kronecker`, so it adds no incompatible parallel API. At most the file duplicates theorems, which this rubric excludes. I found no justified finding. The remaining uncertainty is whether other Mathlib files hold a noncommutative Kronecker-unit result. My searches for the relevant lemma names found none.
